clue.text: Get set to see such plays

definitions.text: Get set to see such plays

parts.words: Get set to see such plays
parts.note: the set is a television receiver, which you need in order to watch drama broadcast on the small screen

explanation.surface: An urging to get ready before going to the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get set' reads like 'get ready', but the set is a TV set.
explanation.definitionFit: Plays shown on a television screen have been broadcast that way.

clue.text: Subject to Bobby taking one in

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the policeman takes the letter for one inside him, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a bobby is a British policeman, a PC (police constable)
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Something that applies to a policeman as he takes one person into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject to' looks like one phrase, but 'Subject' alone is the definition and 'to' gives its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the theme or matter under discussion.

clue.text: Wycliffe's man seen to sprawl over a road

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another comes before it

parts.note: to sprawl lazily is to loll

explanation.surface: A follower of a medieval reformer is spotted lounging across a highway.
explanation.walkthrough: Lollards were followers of John Wycliffe, the 14th-century English church reformer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lollards were the followers of the reformer John Wycliffe.

clue.text: So virulent an attack by three in civil disturbance

indicators.note: the group of three is placed inside the jumbled letters
a disturbance throws the letters of civil into disorder

parts.note: a group of three is a trio

explanation.surface: A savage attack made by three people during civil unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbance' scrambles CIVIL into VILIC, and 'in' sets the trio inside it. 'an attack by' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitriolic means bitterly scathing, as caustic as sulphuric acid.

clue.text: Curry — it isn't cooked first here in the house

indicators.note: the jumbled letters come first, before the next piece
letters that are cooked are doctored or falsified, so rearranged

parts.note: to curry a horse is to groom it with a comb

explanation.surface: A remark that the curry has not yet been made, set in a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' turns IT ISN'T into SITTIN, followed by GROOM. 'Curry' looks like food; it is the verb for brushing a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitting room is a lounge, one of the rooms of a home.

clue.text: Does so skilled a hand have fish fingers?

definitions.text: Does so skilled a hand have fish fingers?

parts.words: Does so skilled a hand have fish fingers?
parts.note: an expert is called by a word for a flatfish followed by hand, so the question asks whether such an expert has fishy fingers

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about whether an expert's hands are made of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'dab hand' is British slang for an expert; a dab is also a small flatfish.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a flatfish and, in 'dab hand', a mark of expertise.

clue.text: Girl in charge? This law would forbid it

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally or Sarah

explanation.surface: A woman takes charge, against a law forbidding just that.
explanation.walkthrough: Salic law barred women from succeeding to a throne, so it would forbid a girl in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: The Salic law of Frankish origin excluded females from inheriting the crown.

clue.text: Meals organized in Witchville, Mass.

indicators.note: the letters of meals are organized into a new order

explanation.surface: Food being arranged in a town in Massachusetts.
explanation.walkthrough: Salem, Massachusetts, is famous for its witch trials of 1692.
explanation.definitionFit: The town in Massachusetts is notorious for its seventeenth-century witch trials.

clue.text: Like the overtures made by boy to girl

parts.note: Leo is a boy's name
Nora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Romantic advances made by a young man to a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overtures' look like romantic approaches; they are Beethoven's three Leonora overtures for his opera Fidelio.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven wrote several overtures named after the heroine of his opera Fidelio.

clue.text: Anxious to be involved

definitions.meaning: having a part or interest in something

explanation.surface: Being worried about getting mixed up in something.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both worried and implicated or taking part.

clue.text: Garment for an adult, not a ruddy infant!

parts.note: a face that is not ruddy is pale
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: Clothing meant for a grown-up, not for a red-faced baby.
explanation.walkthrough: A paletot is a loose overcoat; the exclamation plays on it as an adult's garment, not a pale tot.
explanation.definitionFit: A paletot is a loose outer coat or overcoat.

clue.text: Everybody in favour of air transport

indicators.note: everybody is placed inside the word for a favour

parts.note: a boon is a favour or blessing
everybody means all

explanation.surface: Everyone is in support of travelling by air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in favour of' looks like one phrase meaning supporting; it splits into a container indicator and a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot-air balloon is an early means of flight.

clue.text: Covering of fur perhaps one's seen on this animal

parts.note: a coat of fur covers an animal's body
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Fur covering an animal's body.
explanation.walkthrough: The coati is a long-snouted raccoon relative of the Americas.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a South American mammal of the raccoon family.

clue.text: Yacht-club chief having lost gold in the first place is put out

indicators.note: the word in goes at the front, before the rest

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the club head loses something, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: a commodore is the president of a yacht club
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: A sailing club's president, having lost gold, is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the first place' looks like 'originally'; it puts IN first. COMMODORE minus OR leaves COMMODE.
explanation.definitionFit: To incommode someone is to inconvenience or trouble them.

clue.text: Church heads its modern form ecumenical

definitions.note: an adjective for the whole Christian world, standing for the noun

indicators.note: the church abbreviation heads the rest, coming first
a new form of the letters of its modern rearranges them

explanation.surface: Church leaders adopt their modern ecumenical style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' rearranges ITS MODERN. 'heads' looks like church leaders but says the church abbreviation goes first; 'ecumenical' stands in for the whole Christian world.
explanation.definitionFit: Christendom is the worldwide body of Christians, the universal church.

clue.text: Cain's land of sleep?

parts.note: Genesis sends Cain to a land east of Eden whose name is also the playful name for sleep

explanation.surface: A question about where the biblical Cain went to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: Cain dwelt in the land of Nod; 'the land of Nod' is also a jocular term for sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical land shares its name with a dozing motion of the head.

clue.text: Part of a helmet that's not acquainted only with war, it's said

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken, so the sound of it counts, not the spelling

parts.note: someone not acquainted only with war also knows peace

explanation.surface: A piece of armour for someone who has seen more than just fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knows peace', said aloud, sounds like NOSEPIECE, the nasal guard on a helmet.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosepiece is the guard on a helmet protecting the nose.

clue.text: Conjuring display by a French saint tomorrow

parts.note: Saint Leger was a seventh-century French bishop
demain is French for tomorrow, with French carried over

explanation.surface: A magic show put on by a French saint the next day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' serves both pieces: St Léger, and demain, French for tomorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Legerdemain is sleight of hand, the trickery of a stage magician.

clue.text: Cover for my retirement, could, it be, I wondered?

indicators.note: the question hints that the letters could be something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether something could be a blanket for bedtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' looks like leaving work; it is going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a quilt filled with down, covering a bed.

clue.text: Ill-fated report of transit of a heavenly body

definitions.text: report of transit of a heavenly body
definitions.meaning: a news item saying that a celestial object has passed across

explanation.surface: An unlucky astronomical observation.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo and Juliet are lovers thwarted by the stars, doomed; also a sun passing overhead.

clue.text: This harp in the wind section?

definitions.text: This harp in the wind section?

parts.words: This harp in the wind section?
parts.note: a harp sounded by the breeze rather than fingers, so it belongs among wind instruments, named after the Greek god of winds

explanation.surface: A harp oddly seated among the wind instruments of an orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aeolian harp is played by the wind blowing across its strings; Aeolus was god of winds.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after Aeolus, ruler of winds, the instrument sounds when air blows across it.

clue.text: Partly consumed food the French nobleman rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: duc is French for duke

explanation.surface: A French aristocrat sends back food he has half eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: Cud is food a cow brings back up to chew again.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruminants regurgitate half-digested fodder to chew again.

clue.text: One of two delightful girls Macheath could 'be happy with

definitions.text: One of two delightful girls Macheath could 'be happy with

parts.words: One of two delightful girls Macheath could 'be happy with
parts.note: quotes the Beggar's Opera song in which the highwayman sings how happy he could be with either sweetheart, were the other away

explanation.surface: A highwayman torn between two women.
explanation.walkthrough: In Gay's The Beggar's Opera, Macheath sings 'How happy could I be with either, were t'other dear charmer away!'
explanation.definitionFit: The song calls each of Macheath's two sweethearts a dear delightful one.

clue.text: A little wait, we hear, after the professional agenda

indicators.note: the sounded piece comes after the professional

parts.note: pro is short for professional

indicators.note: the word wait is heard as its soundalike for heaviness

parts.note: wait is heard as weight, and a little weight is a gram, which is said the same as the longer spelling

explanation.surface: A short delay after the expert sets out the agenda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wait, we hear' stands for weight, so 'A little wait' is a small unit of weight, entered in its British spelling. 'after' puts it behind the professional.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme is a schedule or plan of events.

clue.text: Eau de. Cologne, namely?

parts.note: read as French for the water of Cologne, which is the great river flowing through that German city

explanation.surface: A question about the perfume named after Cologne.
explanation.walkthrough: Cologne stands on the Rhine, so the city's 'eau' is that river.
explanation.definitionFit: The great German river flows through Cologne, giving that city its water.

clue.text: How Thespians respond to the stimulus of an encore?

definitions.text: How Thespians respond to the stimulus of an encore?

parts.words: How Thespians respond to the stimulus of an encore?
parts.note: when applause calls them back on stage, performers do their piece once more, while the clue also describes any response to a stimulus

explanation.surface: Actors' behaviour when the audience demands more.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as RE-ACT, 'act again', which is what actors do for an encore; react also means respond to a stimulus.
explanation.definitionFit: To react is to respond to a stimulus, and to re-act is to perform again.

clue.text: In article it appeared this used to decimate the crop

definitions.text: this used to decimate the crop

indicators.note: the word it goes into the article

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper item reports a scheme that cut harvests drastically.
explanation.walkthrough: A tithe was a tenth of produce paid to the church: 'decimate' in its literal sense of taking a tenth.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a levy of one tenth of a farm's produce paid to the church.

clue.text: Journalist provided one church building

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist
provided means if
one is the Roman numeral I
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A newspaperman supplied a single church building.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large, imposing structure.

clue.text: Some use a receiver of audio-frequencies

definitions.text: Some use a receiver of audio-frequencies

parts.words: Some use a receiver of audio-frequencies
parts.note: everyone hears through the organ of hearing; the letters also sit across use a receiver

explanation.surface: People listening with a device for picking up sound.
explanation.walkthrough: The receiver of sound waves is the human organ of hearing; the letters also run across 'usE A Receiver'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ear is the organ that picks up sound.

clue.text: Down-trodden character used to clean shoes

definitions.meaning: a person meekly letting others walk all over them
a mat at the entrance for wiping feet

explanation.surface: A downtrodden person who cleans other people's shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A doormat is wiped by boots at the threshold, and figuratively a person others trample.

clue.text: Bondsman set free by Irene

indicators.note: letters set free are released from their order, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A slave given his freedom by a woman named Irene.
explanation.walkthrough: ERNIE is the machine that draws the winning numbers for British Premium Bonds, a state savings scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: The number-generating machine picks winners in the UK's Premium Bond lottery.

clue.text: Gipsy gentleman takes any railway entering the capital

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the capital city

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Romani man takes any train into the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: A Romany rye, as in George Borrow's novel, is a gentleman who befriends Gypsies.
explanation.definitionFit: Romany rye is the Romani term for a gentleman, used by George Borrow.
